name: Bert
summary: A bert is an erne taken on your partner's side of the court. You cross behind them, go around the far kitchen, and volley the ball they were about to play. It wins the point outright when it works and leaves two thirds of the court empty when it does not, which makes it the least forgiving shot in the game.
whenToUse: The opponents are dinking cross-court to your partner and have stopped watching you.
Your partner can see you coming, or you have already agreed a signal.
The ball will arrive at net height on their sideline, not at their feet.
You are far enough ahead to spend a point finding out.
howTo: Signal or call it, so your partner slides across to cover the side you are leaving.
Start from behind your partner, never in front. Crossing through their swing is how paddles meet faces.
Cross early and land completely outside the sideline, clear of the kitchen.
Punch the volley down at the nearer opponent's feet.
Keep moving through. Your partner has your half and you now have theirs.
commonMistakes: Crossing in front of your partner while they are already swinging.
Going without telling them, which leaves the whole court open when the ball goes the other way.
Attempting it on a ball below net height, where the only shot available is a dink you travelled ten feet to play.
Doing it twice in one game. Once it has been seen, the counter is a straight dink into the space you left.

drills.name: Called berts
drills.description: Two of you at the kitchen against one feeder, dinking cross-court. You must call it out loud before you move; if the feeder hears the call in time they change direction and you have to recover.
